title: A hiring table at a bicycle repair shop: a lower wage, a higher price and derived demand
scenario: Spokewell Cycles (invented) repairs bicycles and sells each repair for \$4 in a perfectly competitive market. It hires mechanics in a perfectly competitive labor market at a wage of \$30 a day. The table shows the number of repairs it completes each day with different numbers of mechanics.

stimulus.title: Mechanics and repairs at Spokewell Cycles

table.caption: Repairs completed per day at the invented Spokewell Cycles (invented data for practice)

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the marginal revenue product of the fourth mechanic. Show your work.

rubric.point: \$24 a day, with work shown: MP = 40 - 34 = 6 repairs, and MRP = 6 × \$4

parts.sample: The fourth mechanic's marginal product is 40 - 34 = 6 repairs. MRP = MP × P = 6 × \$4 = \$24 a day.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: The market wage for mechanics falls to \$20 a day. Identify the number of mechanics Spokewell now hires to maximize profit.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain your answer to B(i) using marginal revenue product and marginal resource cost.

rubric.point: The fourth mechanic's MRP (\$24) is greater than the MRC of \$20 (the wage), while the fifth mechanic's MRP (3 × \$4 = \$12) is less than \$20, so hiring stops at 4
accept: MRP of the 4th = \$24 > \$20 and MRP of the 5th = \$12 < \$20

parts.sample: A profit-maximizing firm hires while MRP is at least MRC, and in a competitive labor market MRC equals the wage, now \$20. The MRPs are \$40, \$56, \$40, \$24 and \$12. The fourth mechanic adds \$24, more than \$20, but the fifth adds only 3 × \$4 = \$12, less than \$20, so Spokewell hires 4.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: Instead, the wage stays at \$30 a day, and the market price of a repair rises to \$6. Identify whether Spokewell now hires the fourth mechanic, and explain using numbers.

rubric.point: Yes: at \$6 the fourth mechanic's MRP is 6 × \$6 = \$36, more than the \$30 wage (the fifth's is 3 × \$6 = \$18, less than \$30)

parts.sample: Yes. A higher price raises the MRP of every mechanic. The fourth mechanic's MRP is now 6 × \$6 = \$36, more than the \$30 wage, so hiring that mechanic adds to profit. (The fifth mechanic's MRP, 3 × \$6 = \$18, is still below \$30.)

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Explain why Spokewell's demand for mechanics is called a derived demand.

rubric.point: Spokewell hires mechanics only because customers buy repairs: its demand for mechanics comes from (is derived from) the demand for the repairs they produce
accept: the demand for labor depends on the demand for the product the labor makes

parts.sample: Spokewell does not want mechanics for their own sake; it hires them to produce repairs that customers buy. So its demand for mechanics depends on the demand for repairs, through the price of a repair in MRP = MP × P: if the demand for repairs rises, so does the demand for mechanics.
